results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 36 unit summaries agree with the controlling idea of the spec paragraph each is aligned to (p01 to p36, in order); the KEY POINTS callout matches no spec paragraph, as page format.

The outliner marked four units as holding two ideas: Two Disciplines ¶2 (four elements / four levers), Three Scarce Capacities ¶4 (AI as second force / what Speculative means), How to Read the Evidence ¶4 (the tiers / how the three sets differ) and ¶5 (dated / living and AI-assisted). In each the two halves are the two parts of the one controlling idea the spec declares for that paragraph (p10, p17, p28, p29; the decision log records p17's gloss and p29's living-book sentence as deliberate), so the draft holds what the spec asks and no more. Note for the author: p29 is the loosest of the four; the AI-assistance disclosure is joined to the dating rule only by 'the text is provisional'.

Each section does what its advances_thesis declares: who (the two readers J1 addresses), disciplines (J1, J7 stated), capacities (J2, J5, J6 stated, J6 with its label), corvane (J5's running example), parts (where each of J1 to J7 is argued), routing (the four levers as a reading method), evidence (the AI labels J6 requires), anchors (where the product and engineering sources meet: planning, decision rights, metrics). No unit argues something outside its section's declared contribution.

Every evidence item is given and interpreted: the Corvane scenario (p01 explained by p02; p13 'made both mistakes'; p15 'What had run out was verification'), Morieux and Tollman (given as the reason behaviour follows structure), the three team-size sentences (each followed by what kind it is and what weight it deserves). All five tables are introduced and read: the two-readers table ('how to use a chapter either way'), the disciplines table (followed by Corvane making both mistakes), the routing table (columns explained before it), the six-kinds table (followed by a worked example), the anchors table ('I state the tension and take a position'). No figures or block quotations.

All 35 declared transition_in relationships are expressed at their boundaries, for example 'You have probably lived through a version of it' (similarity), 'That explanation is the book's claim' (elaboration), 'System design says what to change. It does not say for whom' (additional support), 'With these three, the opening puzzle can be solved' (example), 'You do not have to read in order' (contrast), 'The table tells you where to look; the next question is how far to trust what you find there' (sequence), 'Everything on this page comes down to one habit' (conclusion). Two notes, neither a failure: p16 is declared cause_effect and the draft writes it as instance-to-rule ('Corvane's case is one instance of a rule'), which is what the transition's own carries_over and introduces describe; the anchors section carries 'sources' over in its first sentence without naming them as one of the six kinds (flow reader B inferred the link, reader A saw it).

results.draft_locus: Three Scarce Capacities: Attention, Judgment and Verification ¶2
results.quote: Five platform engineers did this for eleven teams.
results.finding: Both flow readers could not reconcile this with the opening's 'three of them waited for every launch on one platform team': were three teams held up or all eleven, and if three, why did the company-wide median move to 19 days? Both went back to the opening and stayed unsure. The scenario ledger has the fact that reconciles them (all eleven teams needed the platform team for some launches, three for every launch); the draft gives the two figures and never the link. Reader A item 3.1, rated (a).

results.draft_locus: Corvane, the Company the Book Follows ¶1
results.quote: Corvane has now appeared three times, each time as a structure that stayed after its constraint had moved

results.draft_locus: Three Scarce Capacities: Attention, Judgment and Verification ¶4
results.quote: building something took most of a team's attention, so attention was the limit
results.finding: Attention was defined four paragraphs earlier as 'how much a team can hold in mind well enough to change it safely', which runs out 'when a team owns more than it can understand'. Here it is what building uses up, which both readers read as effort or time. Both went back to the definition and could not match the two uses; each assumed a looser sense. The claim that AI moves the limit away from attention rests on this sentence, and the sentence does not connect to the page's own definition. The gloss is the draft's wording (the spec asks only for 'cheap implementation shifts the limit from attention toward judgment and verification'), though the journal thesis has the same compression. Reader A item 3.5, rated (a).

results.finding: The page opens with a puzzling scenario (Corvane hires from 45 to 95 engineers and ships less), turns to the reader's own experience, and states the claim in the third paragraph. No dictionary definition, no history of management, no restatement of the title, no placeholder opening.

'Where to Go Next' does not merely restate the page, apologise or open a new argument: it reduces the page to one habit, returns to Corvane and gives two ways on. The one new fact (Corvane in 2028 asking whether to hire engineers at all) is the callback the spec declares.

Synthesis: 'Everything on this page comes down to one habit. Before you change an organization, ask which capacity is scarce and for whom the change is made', with the parts and the labels placed under it. So-what: 'your next hiring plan or reorganization starts with what is scarce and with how you would know that the change worked.' The take-away (routing table or read on) and the hand-off link follow.

'Corvane's leaders asked how many engineers to hire, when the useful question was what had run out. The book ends with the same company in 2028, asking whether to hire engineers at all' returns to the opening paragraph's hiring wave, as the spec's callback declares.

The cold reader of the introduction alone predicted all eight roadmap promises in the declared order (readers; disciplines and capacities; Corvane; the eleven parts; the routing table; the evidence labels and the main sources), the kind of evidence (an illustrative case, labelled) and the tone. It grouped disciplines with capacities and labels with sources, as the roadmap's sentences do, and did not predict that the capacities would be used to explain the hiring wave; neither changes the order or the content it expected.

The cold reader stated the argument (a designable system; system design and product thinking; attention, judgment and verification; a structure right only for its constraint, which growth and AI move) and listed the eleven parts in order with the subject of each: Foundations, Topology, Product, Engineering, Leadership, Alignment, Talent, Health, Culture, Evolution, AI. This matches the expected answer.

The cold reader opened team-types first, 'which decides whether a platform team is justified', then platforms-and-developer-experience 'on how to run one and judge it': the expected answer. The page is consistent with it: the platform-team row has team-types under 'Open first' and 'Then [[platforms-and-developer-experience]]' in the third column, and the paragraph above the table says to open the second-column chapter first and that the third column is a prerequisite or a chapter to read afterwards. The reader noted that the row's two clauses (whether / how to run) are what kept it from going to the platforms chapter by name.
The first paragraph is the Corvane scenario. The page does not open with a definition of 'organization', a history of management or a restatement of the title.
